question: Should an OpenClaw upgrade preserve existing OpenShell sandbox identities when the generated-name format changes, or is creating a replacement remote sandbox an accepted compatibility break?
rationale: The answer determines whether the PR needs legacy lookup/adoption or a deliberately documented recreation path; code review cannot safely choose between preservation and intentional state replacement.

options.title: Preserve existing identities
options.body: Add a narrow legacy-name lookup or migration path, prove that existing remote workspaces and cleanup continue to target the original sandbox, then create bounded names only for new scopes.

options.title: Accept explicit recreation
options.body: Approve the identity break only with user-facing upgrade guidance and proof that operators can identify, preserve, and intentionally retire old remote sandboxes.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing identities
recommendation.body: Add a narrow legacy-name lookup or migration path, prove that existing remote workspaces and cleanup continue to target the original sandbox, then create bounded names only for new scopes.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the remote OpenShell lifecycle and canonical-workspace behavior that defines the upgrade contract.
